sentences.text:
This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:
 ORDER
This is first bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure filed on behalf of the applicant for grant of bail, pending the trial.

The applicant is in custody since 30.11.2022 in connection with Crime No.837/2022, registered at P.S.-Gotegaon, District - Narsinghpur (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 323,
506/34 and 377 of IPC and Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
As per the prosecution story, on 29.11.2022 complainant i.e. wife of the applicant lodged an FIR alleging that her marriage was performed with the applicant on 02.05.2021.

Her father had given sufficient dowry in marriage but after marriage applicant and his parents, sister started to harass and torture her in connection with demand of dowry of Rs.10.00 lac and a four wheeler.

sentences.text: Her husband used to commit unnatural sex with her causing lot of discomfort.
FIR was registered.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.

He had filed an application under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act before the competent Court for Restitution of the Conjugal Rights but his wife does not want to remain with him due to which she has lodged a false FIR.
He shall abide by all the conditions whatsoever imposed by the Court.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant be released on bail pending the trial.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the grant of bail to the applicant.
In this case, FIR has been lodged on 29.11.2022.
Husband had filed an application for Restitution of the Conjugal Rights before the Family Court on 13.09.2022.
Thus, it is apparent that there is some matrimonial dispute between the two.
In this case after investigation, charge sheet has been filed.
Trial of the case will take considerable time.

Therefore, having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre trial detention of the applicant is not warranted.
Consequently, this first bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

It is directed that applicant - Rishabh Kori be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE Jasleen Rishabh Kori vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80032374/
